cards.text: Jerusalem is in danger, and Jeremiah the prophet has been telling all the people what the LORD says about it. Four officials hear about it: Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jucal and Pashhur. The message starts like this: whoever stays in this city will die by sword and famine and plague.

cards.question: Whoever stays in Jerusalem will die. So who does the LORD's message say will live?
Jeremiah also tells the people the LORD says the army of Babylon's king will never capture Jerusalem.

cards.text: So the officials go to Zedekiah, king of Judah. They say Jeremiah's words are discouraging the warriors who remain in the city, and all the people too.

cards.question: What do the officials tell King Zedekiah should happen to Jeremiah?

cards.text: Now it's up to the king, the man with the crown and the throne. Surely HE makes the call. Right?

cards.question: What does King Zedekiah tell the officials about Jeremiah?

cards.text: The KING says he can do NOTHING to stop them, so they take Jeremiah to the cistern of Malchiah, the king's son, in the courtyard of the guard. Friend, that's a boss telling his staff, "I'd stop you, but y'all don't listen to me anyway."

cards.question: How do the officials get Jeremiah down into the cistern?

answers.text: They lower him in a basket
They lead him down some steps

cards.question: The cistern has no water in it, only ___, and Jeremiah sinks down into it.

cards.text: So Jeremiah is sinking at the bottom of a muddy pit. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer under paper and dust, and I'm telling you right now: I had it GOOD.
Then Ebed-melech the Cushite, a court official in the royal palace, hears what happened. While the king is sitting at the Gate of Benjamin, Ebed-melech goes out from the palace to talk to him.

cards.question: Ebed-melech tells King Zedekiah that these men have acted wickedly in all they've done to Jeremiah.
Ebed-melech says Jeremiah will starve to death in that cistern. Why?

answers.text: There is no more bread in the city
The officials took away his food
The guards are not allowed to feed him

cards.question: King Zedekiah turns Ebed-melech down and leaves Jeremiah in the cistern.

cards.text: Instead, the king tells Ebed-melech to take thirty men and pull Jeremiah the prophet out of the cistern before he dies. THIRTY men for one prophet? That's not a rescue, friend, that's a PARADE.
Ebed-melech takes the men to a place below the palace storehouse and grabs old rags and worn-out clothes. Then he lowers them with ropes down to Jeremiah in the cistern.

cards.question: Ebed-melech calls down to Jeremiah to put the rags and worn-out clothes under his arms. Why?

answers.text: To keep warm in the mud

cards.question: Once they pull Jeremiah up out of the cistern, he is set free from the courtyard of the guard.

cards.text: Then King Zedekiah sends for Jeremiah the prophet and meets him at the third entrance to the house of the LORD. He's got a question, and he tells Jeremiah, "Do not hide anything from me."

cards.question: Before he answers, Jeremiah tells King Zedekiah what will happen if he tells him. What?

answers.text: The king will surely put him to death
The king will throw him back in the cistern
The king will send him off to Babylon

cards.text: Zedekiah doesn't back off. He swears to Jeremiah in secret, as surely as the LORD lives. Friend, the KING is whispering.

cards.question: What does King Zedekiah secretly swear to Jeremiah?

answers.text: He will not kill him or hand him over
He will set him free from the guard
He will do whatever the LORD says

cards.text: So Jeremiah gives him the word of the LORD God of Hosts, the God of Israel. It's an if-then, and the first "if" is surrender.

cards.question: If King Zedekiah surrenders to the officers of Babylon's king, what does the LORD say will happen?

answers.text: He will live and the city will not burn
He will live but the city will burn
He will be carried away to Babylon

cards.question: If Zedekiah does not surrender, the LORD says Jerusalem will still not be burned down.

cards.text: But Zedekiah has a fear, and he lays it right out on the table for Jeremiah.

cards.question: Who does King Zedekiah tell Jeremiah he's afraid of?

answers.text: The Jews who deserted to the Chaldeans
The prophets who spoke against Jeremiah

cards.question: Jeremiah tells King Zedekiah the Chaldeans will not hand him over to those deserters.

cards.text: Jeremiah tells him to obey the voice of the LORD, so it may go well with him and he may live. But if he refuses to surrender, Jeremiah shares what the LORD has shown him.
All the women left in the palace of Judah's king will be brought out to the officials of Babylon's king. And those women will say something about Zedekiah's trusted friends.

cards.question: What do the palace women say Zedekiah's trusted friends did to him?

answers.text: Fought beside him to the end
Paid a ransom to save him

cards.text: The women also say Zedekiah's feet sank into the mire, and friend, not long ago Jeremiah was the one sinking into the mud.

cards.question: Jeremiah says that if Zedekiah refuses, his family will be taken but Zedekiah himself will escape.

cards.text: Then Zedekiah warns Jeremiah not to let anyone know about this conversation, or he will die. It's a group chat with ONE rule, friend: nobody screenshots.

cards.question: If the officials demand to know what Jeremiah and the king talked about, what does Zedekiah tell Jeremiah to say?

answers.text: He asked not to be sent back to Jonathan's house to die
He came to warn the king about the deserters in Babylon
He came to pray for the king and the people of the city

cards.question: The officials question Jeremiah, and he gives them the exact words the king told him to say. Why do they say no more to him?

answers.text: No one had overheard the conversation
The king ordered them to leave him alone
Ebed-melech stepped in to defend him

cards.question: How long does Jeremiah remain in the courtyard of the guard?

answers.text: Until the day Jerusalem is captured
Until the day Zedekiah sets him free
Until the day the officials release him

cards.text: We're stopping here, friend, but don't take your apron off. This story is still in the oven.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing from the passage. It cites Jeremiah 38:4, but it only repeats that the decision is now the king's. Its sarcastic setup ('Surely HE makes the call. Right?') also tells the baker the king won't decide, which rules out the wrong answer 'Leave him to me' on card 7.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card doesn't move the passage forward. It only builds anticipation, and no new part of the text is told.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The joke line ('I'd stop you, but y'all don't listen to me anyway') gives Zedekiah a reason and a wish to stop them that the text doesn't give. Jeremiah 38:5 says only 'since the king can do nothing to stop you.'

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This card is a recap. 'So Jeremiah is sinking at the bottom of a muddy pit' repeats Jeremiah 38:6, which cards 8 to 10 already covered, and then adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

No card tells the second half of Jeremiah 38:15: 'And even if I give you advice, you will not listen to me.' This is an important detail about Zedekiah, who asks for the truth but won't act on it, and it sets up the rest of the conversation.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates this stop: 7 of 11 choice cards are multiple choice, 4 are true or false, and none are fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This closing card is only the 'story isn't over' line, which is allowed because Jeremiah 38:28 is asked on card 19. It still cites Jeremiah 38:28, even though it tells nothing from that verse.
findings.question: What should the verses field be on a story card that is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse: the passage's last verse, the stop's range, or something else?
